tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, Reuse (extract before the second use), shared files and Tool facts; Decisions 3-4, 7-9 and 13; Acceptance evidence 3 (Lock and shared test seams), Security impact and Rollout order. FIRST extract the lock and atomicWrite/link/mode checks from cli/write-install.ts into cli/lock.ts and cli/safe-write.ts, with their tests, and migrate init. Preserve ownership-by-content release and recorded signals. Extend lock with Decision 3's five-line pid/nonce/host/started/command content and environment-independent process identity behind injected process.kill/platform/hostname/three-/proc-read/files seams. Never run ps, spawn a process or format a time. Linux identity is linux:<boot_id>:<pid-namespace-inode>:<field22-starttime-ticks>; parse stat after its last ')' to support command names with spaces/parentheses. Invalid/unreadable identity is '-'; macOS uses '-' without reading /proc. Implement every stale-judgement table row: same host/boot/namespace permits ESRCH or a running pid with valid different ticks; same boot/different namespace never breaks; different boot breaks; mixed Linux/'-' never breaks; '-'/ '-' breaks only ESRCH. EPERM/unreadable live stat/doubt refuse. Break under wx 0600 .pulse-init.lock.break, byte-equal reread, unlink/own wx/directory fsync; refuse foreign-host, legacy, live, invalid and changing locks and always release an owned break file. Acquire before guard/journal/upgrade.json/recovery reads. Rewrite docs/cli.md's stale-lock guidance for init, token rotate and upgrade, including the Linux/macOS identity rules, shared-host/manual checks and both lock files; explain unsupported shared directories on distinct machines with one hostname. Add matching docs assertions now. Environment fixtures and real-/proc Linux child-process tests belong here; T6 captures Linux identity output and the explicit non-Linux skip (no ps evidence). safe-write.ts owns the single validated-state reader/durable writer, safe writes and archive finalization with file and directory fsync. One injected file seam exposes mkdir/open/read/write/file-fsync/rename/directory-fsync/unlink and records creates, token-file lstat/reads and all persistence events in the same ordered log as fake Docker. It supports T5's power-loss view: only parent-fsynced entries and file-fsynced content survive; T5 owns the crash-prefix checks and broken variants. It must preserve observable on-disk renames when a later fsync throws, offer ONE validated read-back after a failed state write without retry, and simulate errors or hard kills without cleanup. Consumer reconciliation/action tables stay in T4/T5. Extend cli/docker.ts's sole spawn for input/stdinFd/stdoutFd, default ignored stdin, fd bytes and binary-named ENOENT (Docker remains exit 3, gh becomes exit 1). Return checkConfig's already-parsed effective Compose model in Project, with own()/isObj readers; preserve override/--no-interpolate and one resolution call. FIRST extract checkVolumes' existing inspect-and-two-label comparison into one exported cli/docker.ts function with tests returning missing, owned, foreign or inspect error. Keep the guard skipping missing volumes and rejecting foreign ones; T5 consumes this function to REQUIRE existing owned snapshot volumes before mutation and around helpers, without duplicating label checks. Reuse INSTALL_LABEL from cli/render-compose.ts. Export and reuse PULSE_IMAGE/assertPin from cli/services.ts with runtime-assembled shape fixtures. Extend parsePs for full ID and readyz/waitReady for container targeting; no duplicate guard, poller, pin pattern or spawn. cli/api-call.ts owns constant API_SCRIPT (stdin JSON, fixed localhost URL, 10 s fetch, 11 s unref'd exit 70, redirect:error, 1 MiB cap) and the timingSafeEqual file-comparison script (stdin expected secret, same/different only, 10 s bound). The client ending is never a server barrier: implement no settle process scan or SETTLE_SCRIPT. Extend cli/test/fake-docker.ts as the sole fake spawn with input/fds/signals/full ids/states/labels and named stop-at-step hooks. Prepare API stop/start/inspect, per-volume inspect answers, -v creating a missing volume WITHOUT labels, and helpers surviving client death for T4/T5. Model Docker client and daemon separately with pending create/start/run requests deliverable after a killed run, inert created containers, rm -f ending all phases, and start of a removed id failing No such container; T5 owns the shared two-step launcher, pending-client and helper-phase matrices. T4 owns server-write fault matrices. Each shared module states its ownership and tests its variants.

Before every rotate/create POST durably mark inFlight in requested/replacing respectively. Unanswered write recovery is the Decision 8 Barrier, NOT a client-process scan: exactly one API container, compose stop --timeout 10 api, inspect Running=false/Pid=0, start api/waitReady, durable inFlight:null, print restart duration. Run before any readback, sweep or next POST while disk marker is set; matching staging confirmation is the sole exception because that answer was parsed. A barrier failure keeps marker, exits 1 with api-may-be-stopped/rerun-or-pulse-up hint, sends no further API calls, and reruns the barrier. Normal parsed rotation restarts no api. Rejected answers need no first-run barrier; clear marker in the next state/drop. Classify readback in precedence order: gone for 404, non-null revokedAt or expired expiresAt REGARDLESS of rotatedAt; changed only for an active token with changed rotatedAt; same only for an active token with unchanged rotatedAt; unknown otherwise. Readback determines retry/drop/replacement/hold exactly as Decision 8; at most 2 rotate POSTs per item/run. Replacing entry only for changed rotatedAt OR parsed ok rotate whose stage-error reconcile found no staging file. Persist replacementName/revokeTokenId before create. Replacing begins with marker-triggered barrier, then exact-name orphan sweep only after reconcile found no held replacement. Unconfirmed revoke prevents create. AFTER that sweep and immediately BEFORE EVERY replacement create, reread the lost token through the SAME ordered classifier: changed permits create; gone drops item/later requested items and exits 1 with token <id> was revoked or expired; no replacement was made; same/unknown retains replacing/inFlight:null and exits 1 with no create. Do not undo revocations or expiry even if rotatedAt changed; admin revoked bearer yields 401/unknown and recovery needs another admin. Create parsed 201 stages; rejected clears marker/exits 1 without another create; ambiguous or lost staging returns to barrier+sweep before another create. At most 2 creates per item/run; before limit exit finish the last barrier/sweep, leave replacing/inFlight:null and no unheld replacement. Final sweep in switched excludes activeTokenId, then revoke original, then delete journal. No barrier in switched (inFlight:null). Preserve other names. Fake API holds writes SERVER-SIDE independently of dead clients until stop resolves apply/drop, can schedule mutations after sweep/final sweep/run exit, and runs a post-exit apply to expose unsafe ordering. Do not drive this fake from client lifetime. One fake API also enforces revoked-secret 401, permitted self-revoke and last-admin 409. Probe handoff follows observed-container resume table, retains new id, never rescales old+new; ready/same/2000 ms precede old stop/removal; locations serial. Admin new identity precedes console recreate/readiness/equality/own-file identity. Report inspect-derived W (or unknown if old gone). Only required consumers restart except recovery API barrier. Record signals through durable markers, POST/staging/reconcile, barrier/readback/retry/sweeps/revoke critical sections; act at boundaries with 130. Every hard-kill test retains the old lock and proves automatic stale break BEFORE recovery reads. Wire selector/journal-argument/timeout validation, HELP/COMMANDS/dispatch and stub errors. Command docs/manual equivalents and Token recovery cover staging secrets never manually deleted, reconcile order/errors, both sweeps/revoke guard, outcome rows with gone-before-changed precedence and fresh pre-create readback (no replacement for revoked/expired tokens), barrier API downtime/failure recovery with pulse up, stale lock, extra containers, lost-admin overlap expiry/manual token recovery, standalone exclusions and measured handoff cost. Document bound domains I>=200 and I>700 and separate short-interval estimate per Performance impact. Real 10-minute expiry/continuity stays in T6.

tasks.title: pulse upgrade verifies digests and snapshots existing owned stores durably before switching
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, registry/provenance/snapshot/upgrade, wiring and docs; Decisions 1, 3 and 10-13; Required behavior (upgrade and Help and docs); all upgrade, provenance, mount, snapshot, rollback, helper and lock Counterexamples; Acceptance evidence 2 (production behavior), 3 (Data mounts, Missing and foreign data volumes, Upgrade, Upgrade state writes, Snapshot directory chain, Power loss, Surviving helpers, Pending helper clients, Durable restore, Docs), 5-6; Security impact, Performance impact 3 and Risks. Keep this one snapshot/apply/rollback algorithm with its matrices. Fixed-host injected ghcr.io fetch: numeric stable SemVer, optional-v exact --to without leading zeros/prereleases, <=10 pages, redirect:error, 20 s, 1 MiB, checked OCI index/manifest-list digest. Reject nonempty volumes_from. Export ONE cli/snapshot.ts path normalizer following scripts/check-setup.sh rule8 def norm; normalize slashes/dot/dotdot and /var/run alias. Build paths from volume targets, tmpfs string/list with options stripped at first colon, configs target or /<source>, secrets target or /run/secrets/<source>. Reject every other mount at/below/above a writable volume (including /), while allowing harmless tmpfs/config/secret elsewhere. Require exactly one writable /data on api/notify/console and absent/literal default data paths; reject moved/interpolated variables. Record actual Compose effective-model fixtures with cli/test/record-compose-mounts.sh into cli/test/compose-mounts.json, including Compose version and each override text; retain ONLY services' volumes/tmpfs/configs/secrets/volumes_from/environment and top-level volumes via jq, never images/pins. bun tests read recorded JSON without Docker; assert no ghcr.io or sha256:. Preserve a hand-built tmpfs:[/data] counterexample for Compose versions that reject that input. A volumes-only validator variant must fail recorded tmpfs cases. Sorted deduplicated snapshotVolumes includes all writable sources irrespective of suffix, omits unused/read-only volumes; complete tars keys must equal it. Use T2's shared volume inspector (no second label comparison): every snapshot volume MUST exist with this install's INSTALL_LABEL and project label before provenance, including preview. Missing refuses with data volume <project>_<key> does not exist; run pulse up once before pulse upgrade; see docs/cli.md#upgrade. Null/foreign labels refuse does not belong to this installation; other inspect errors remain failures. The guard's missing-volume skip does NOT satisfy this check. Repeat ownership/existence check right before each CREATE and after each START of EACH snapshot/restore helper and for ALL snapshotVolumes in abort before restart. Around snapshot/abort failure: sweep helpers, keep snapshotting/all archives, no aborted/deletion/start/further helper. Around restore failure: sweep then rollback-failed/restored:false, no start. Fake volumes may disappear and -v creates unlabelled replacements; checks must catch this. Require installed authenticated gh; verify each changed digest within 120 s with repo/signer-workflow/source-ref/deny-self-hosted-runners even in preview, no bypass/re-resolution; pull/write that exact digest. Preview changes 0 files/containers. Apply takes recoverable lock BEFORE guard/state reads. Immediately after guard sweep leftover helpers by existing INSTALL_LABEL+new helper label BEFORE nonterminal-directory refusal, then reject journal/incomplete/unreadable snapshot metadata. Helper sweep: list by both labels, rm -f each full id, list empty; <=3 rounds/30 s, print count when nonzero; failure names ids/recovery link with no state/restore/start. Never rely on Compose down or client kill to end standalone helpers. Label every snapshot/restore helper; use only resolved pinned secrets-init image and Decision 13 restricted network/capabilities. FIRST implement ONE shared helper launcher in cli/snapshot.ts for snapshot and restore: docker create --rm with labels/options and stdin -i only for restore, 30 s bound; require exit0 and exactly one 64-lowerhex id line; ONLY its same live invocation may spawn docker start -a <id> (snapshot stdout fd) or docker start -a -i <id> (restore stdin fd). No production helper docker run and no starting ids found by a sweep. Check volume BEFORE CREATE (create already mounts it), and after start exits. Invalid id/create/start failure triggers sweep and the step's failure path. Model pending client requests separately from containers: late create leaves inert created helper; late start before rm is killed by rm, late start after rm fails No such container; sweeps include --all. A killed-create client cannot cause a later helper phase; tests must prove one-step run variant violates this. A pending create may leave an inert container after an empty sweep and refusal; next sweep removes it. Do not infer daemon completion from client death. Sweep during abort, before first restore, after nonzero/throwing restore spawn before state write, and before EVERY upgrade/abort/rollback up. Before stopping anything, durably create the snapshot directory CHAIN in Decision 13 step4 order: mkdir .pulse-upgrade 0700 when absent, fsync install directory EVEN WHEN .pulse-upgrade already exists, mkdir unique snapshot 0700, fsync .pulse-upgrade, then four-part snapshotting write/fsync snapshot directory. Failure cleans only newly created snapshot contents/directory, keeps pre-existing .pulse-upgrade, exits1/could not create the snapshot directory with 0 stops/helpers; cleanup failure leaves a blocking directory. Snapshot streams each sorted existing owned volume to wx0600 .tar.part, fsync/size/hash/rename/directory fsync; copy Compose with wx0600/file-fsync/snapshot-directory-fsync and verify composeSha256. T5 uses the shared file/fake-spawn log for directory-chain failures and simulated power-loss prefixes, and proves detection with variants omitting each required parent fsync. States snapshotting/applying/done/aborted/rolling-back/restored/rolled-back/rollback-failed with restored boolean and validated external input. Complete boundary is on-disk applying+tars, but only durable applying permits switch.
